question: What does the unloader valve on a plant air compressor do?
options: It raises the receiver pressure above the compressor's rated limit so the stored air can do more work before the compressor has to restart and refill the receiver tank again
It relieves pressure from the compressor head at shutdown or cut-out so the motor can restart without fighting trapped pressure
It drains condensed water from the receiver tank on a timed cycle
It filters oil out of the compressed air before the air dryer unit
correct_answer_text: It relieves pressure from the compressor head at shutdown or cut-out so the motor can restart without fighting trapped pressure

question: Which set of items belongs on a routine storage tank inspection?
options: Only the color of the office paperwork, checking that plant office forms and folders match the color scheme
Only the calibration of the feed pump
Only motor nameplates in the pump room
Tank vents and screens, overflow with flap or screen, coating condition, and signs of ice damage
correct_answer_text: Tank vents and screens, overflow with flap or screen, coating condition, and signs of ice damage

question: A known standard reads well outside its expected range during a routine check. What should the analyst do?
options: Report sample results as usual anyway and note the failed standard in a file that no one reviews until the end of the year for annual audits
Stop, recalibrate or correct the instrument, and recheck the standard before analyzing samples for reporting
Change the standard value on paper
Skip QC checks for the rest of week
correct_answer_text: Stop, recalibrate or correct the instrument, and recheck the standard before analyzing samples for reporting

question: Before entering a manhole, when should the atmosphere be tested?
options: Only after entry is complete and work has begun inside the space for the shift
Before entry and continuously or periodically during entry
Only if a worker inside the space reports a headache, dizziness, or a strong odor
Only once each week for spaces that are entered on a regular daily schedule
correct_answer_text: Before entry and continuously or periodically during entry

question: Which of the following is a point source of contamination?
options: Runoff washing fertilizer off many farm fields
A discharge pipe releasing waste to a stream
Rainfall moving across a large parking area
Seepage from scattered septic systems across a county
correct_answer_text: A discharge pipe releasing waste to a stream

question: A volume of 2 units of a 5,000 mg/L solution is diluted to a total volume of 100 units, using the same volume units throughout. What is the final concentration?

Weekly records show the MCRT climbing steadily from 9 days to 17 days over a month, even though the operator has not changed the wasting rate. Pin floc is starting to appear in the effluent. What is the best action?
options: Decrease the wasting rate, because a rising MCRT means the plant is losing too many solids in the effluent
Increase the wasting rate in small steps to bring the sludge age back down before the old-sludge problems grow
Hold wasting steady and wait, because a higher MCRT always improves settling and effluent clarity over time in the plant over time
Increase the RAS rate, because returning more solids to the basin is the main control over the sludge age
correct_answer_text: Increase the wasting rate in small steps to bring the sludge age back down before the old-sludge problems grow

question: An operator is replacing a UV lamp and grips the new lamp's glass tube with bare hands before sliding it into its sleeve. Why is this poor practice?
options: Bare hands can crack the quartz sleeve as the lamp is inserted
The lamp will not fit into the sleeve if it has been touched first
Oils from skin left on the lamp create hot spots and shorten lamp life, so lamps are handled with clean gloves
Touching the lamp erases its electronic hour record in the controller and also damages the sleeve seals so the lamp can never be used in any other bank at the plant again
correct_answer_text: Oils from skin left on the lamp create hot spots and shorten lamp life, so lamps are handled with clean gloves

question: A washdown hose shows bulges and its couplings are damaged after being stored kinked on a hot floor. What is the correct outcome?
options: Keep using the hose at lower pressure since washdown service is not very demanding
Remove the hose from service and store its replacement coiled in a cool, clean area
Cut out the bulged section and rejoin the hose with a clamp for continued plant use
Store the replacement hose the same way, since heat and kinks do not shorten hose life
correct_answer_text: Remove the hose from service and store its replacement coiled in a cool, clean area

question: An analyst pipettes 5 mL of a 500 mg/L stock solution into a flask and brings the total volume to 250 mL with dilution water. What concentration is the working solution?
options: 10 mg/L
25 mg/L
100 mg/L
correct_answer_text: 10 mg/L

question: What is a key physical property of chlorine gas that shapes how a leak behaves indoors?
options: It is lighter than air and collects at the ceiling
It dissolves instantly in room air with no hazard
It is odorless and colorless at all concentrations
It is heavier than air and collects in low areas
correct_answer_text: It is heavier than air and collects in low areas

question: A raw water holding basin holds 210,000 gallons and raw water flows through it at 500 gpm. What is the detention time in the basin?
A plant treats 0.80 MGD and applies a chlorine dose of 12 mg/L. How many pounds of chlorine are fed per day?
options: 9.60 lb/day
96.00 lb/day
66.72 lb/day
80.06 lb/day
correct_answer_text: 80.06 lb/day

question: A primary clarifier is pumped down only once every three days. By the third day the sludge is gassy, odorous, and clumps of it float to the surface and leave with the effluent. What change is indicated?
options: Pump a much larger amount once a week so the clarifier bottom is scoured completely clean each time
Stop sludge pumping and let the blanket build until the scraper torque alarm forces a complete cleanout
Add the floating sludge back through the scum line so it gets another pass across the clarifier surface
Pump smaller amounts of sludge more frequently so it is removed before it turns septic in the clarifier
correct_answer_text: Pump smaller amounts of sludge more frequently so it is removed before it turns septic in the clarifier

question: A pressure transducer on a force main reads several pounds higher than a test gauge installed at the same point, and the offset is about the same at low and high pressures. What should be done?
options: Replace the pump, since its discharge pressure no longer matches the transducer
Accept the transducer reading, because electronic sensors are always more accurate
Note the difference in the log and wait for the transducer to correct itself in service for at least a full operating season before anyone considers taking it out and sending it in for service
Check and recalibrate the transducer's zero and span, since a steady offset across the range indicates instrument drift
correct_answer_text: Check and recalibrate the transducer's zero and span, since a steady offset across the range indicates instrument drift

question: A calibration column check shows a metering pump delivering much less than its set rate, and the chemical suction tubing is partly plugged with deposits. What is the best interpretation and action?
options: The SCADA system has failed; reboot it
The tank level is too accurate; ignore the test
The restricted suction is reducing feed; clear the plugging and repeat the calibration check to confirm the rate
The pump is delivering correctly because it is still running
correct_answer_text: The restricted suction is reducing feed; clear the plugging and repeat the calibration check to confirm the rate

question: How is alkalinity most correctly described and reported?
options: The water's buffering capacity against pH change, titrated with standard acid and reported as mg/L as CaCO3
The total calcium plus magnesium, reported in NTU after measuring the light scattered by the sample in a turbidimeter cell
The pink color intensity, reported as free chlorine
The weight of dried solids, reported in mg/L as TSS
correct_answer_text: The water's buffering capacity against pH change, titrated with standard acid and reported as mg/L as CaCO3

question: A coworker reaches for a hose to spray water on a leaking chlorine cylinder to knock down the gas. What should you tell the coworker?
options: Spray only the bottom half of the cylinder, keeping the spray away from the valve and fusible plug at the top
Use a fine mist instead of a solid stream
Spray the cylinder only after the room is ventilated
Stop — never apply water to a leaking chlorine cylinder because corrosion can make the leak worse
correct_answer_text: Stop — never apply water to a leaking chlorine cylinder because corrosion can make the leak worse

question: Iron in a source water is most associated with which customer complaint?
options: A strong rotten-egg odor in cold water only
White scale deposits inside water heaters
Red water and staining
Blue-green stains on plumbing fixtures
correct_answer_text: Red water and staining

question: A clarifier with 750 sq ft of surface area receives 900,000 gallons per day. What is its surface loading rate?
options: 120.00 gpd/sq ft
12,000.00 gpd/sq ft
1,200.00 gpd/sq ft
0.83 gpd/sq ft
correct_answer_text: 1,200.00 gpd/sq ft

question: A belt press filtrate suddenly carries much more solids while the polymer dose and feed rate are unchanged. What should the operator check first?
options: The press room lighting schedule
The cake truck scale calibration
Whether polymer conditioning still matches the character of the sludge being fed
The bar screen rake timing
correct_answer_text: Whether polymer conditioning still matches the character of the sludge being fed

question: On a freezing night an RBC is shut down for drive repairs and left sitting still with wet media exposed to the cold air. Why is leaving it stopped a problem?
options: The biomass will grow twice as fast while the shaft is not turning at all
The clarifier will receive too much flow while the contactor is offline
Ice can form on the exposed media, adding weight and damaging the media and shaft when rotation resumes
The wastewater in the tank will lose all of its dissolved oxygen within minutes once the fans stop for even a very short maintenance break
correct_answer_text: Ice can form on the exposed media, adding weight and damaging the media and shaft when rotation resumes

question: Why must a standby generator be exercised regularly under load rather than only started and idled?
options: Idling for one minute fully proves generator capacity
Load testing is done only to use up old fuel, regardless of whether the plant load is actually carried
Testing under load shows it can actually carry the plant's electrical demand during an outage
A generator that starts once never needs testing again
correct_answer_text: Testing under load shows it can actually carry the plant's electrical demand during an outage

question: A cooler arrives at the lab with a bacteriological bottle that has no collection time or location on its label. What is the main problem?
options: The result cannot be reliably tied to where and when it was collected, weakening documentation and defensibility
The missing label will neutralize the chlorine in the bottle and allow bacteria to grow unchecked during transport to the lab
The bottle is no longer sterile solely because the label is incomplete
DPD testing cannot be performed on any unlabeled bottle
correct_answer_text: The result cannot be reliably tied to where and when it was collected, weakening documentation and defensibility

question: After documenting a resident's complaint about a sewer backup, what completes a proper response?
options: Telling the resident that backups are never the utility's concern and that they should call a private plumber for every problem on their street
Closing the complaint as soon as the call ends
Waiting for the resident to call back before checking anything
Investigating the reported location, taking any needed corrective action, and following up so the resident knows the outcome
correct_answer_text: Investigating the reported location, taking any needed corrective action, and following up so the resident knows the outcome

question: What is the main advantage of a reservoir intake tower with ports at several depths?
options: Operators can drain the entire reservoir quickly for cleaning
The tower disinfects water at each depth before it is withdrawn
Operators can choose the depth with the best water quality
The ports remove the need for any treatment after the reservoir
correct_answer_text: Operators can choose the depth with the best water quality

question: What is potassium permanganate used for in a treatment process?
options: As a coagulant that replaces alum and builds large settleable floc in the basins
As a filter medium that strains cysts from water passing through a membrane sheet
As an oxidant that helps convert dissolved iron and manganese for later filtration
As a disinfectant residual that is measured with the DPD test in distribution lines
correct_answer_text: As an oxidant that helps convert dissolved iron and manganese for later filtration

question: The water level upstream of a mechanically cleaned bar screen keeps rising while the level downstream stays normal, and the rake is running almost continuously. What is the best interpretation?
options: Solids are blinding the screen faster than the rake can clear them, so the screenings load or rake operation needs attention
The downstream pumps are drawing the channel down too fast, and the screen itself is operating exactly as designed, regardless of what the screen itself is doing at the time
The grit chamber air rate is too high, which is pushing a surge of water back toward the screen from downstream
The influent has become septic, and the dissolved gas in the wastewater is taking up space in the screen channel
correct_answer_text: Solids are blinding the screen faster than the rake can clear them, so the screenings load or rake operation needs attention

question: A flowmeter on a sludge line keeps plugging and giving erratic readings because rags catch on its internal parts. Which meter type would avoid parts inside the flow stream?
options: A paddlewheel meter with a spinning rotor
A magnetic flowmeter with no moving parts in flow
A turbine meter with bearings inside the pipe housing
A propeller meter driven by the passing sludge
correct_answer_text: A magnetic flowmeter with no moving parts in flow

question: A motor bearing runs hot and grease is weeping from its seals after a worker added several extra shots of grease. What most likely happened?
options: Over-greasing churned the excess grease and overheated the bearing
The bearing was starved because grease blocked the oil feed line
The grease thinned the bearing metal and enlarged the housing bore
Excess grease improved cooling, so heat must come from low voltage
correct_answer_text: Over-greasing churned the excess grease and overheated the bearing

question: A sample shows a free chlorine residual of 0.6 mg/L and a total chlorine residual of 1.0 mg/L. What is the combined residual and what does it represent?
options: 0.4 mg/L, representing only hypochlorous acid
1.6 mg/L, representing chlorine demand
0.6 mg/L, representing inactive chlorine
0.4 mg/L, representing chlorine combined, such as chloramines formed with ammonia
correct_answer_text: 0.4 mg/L, representing chlorine combined, such as chloramines formed with ammonia

question: What is the purpose of lockout and tagout before servicing a pump?
options: To speed up the repair so the pump can return to service without any testing
To prevent unexpected energization or startup while work is performed
To record the pump run hours for the monthly operations report to the state
To keep the pump running at low speed while seals and bearings are replaced
correct_answer_text: To prevent unexpected energization or startup while work is performed

question: During a well inspection an operator finds a cracked sanitary seal and an unscreened vent. Why is this a priority to correct?
options: The well will start producing twice as much water with a higher yield
The pump will start drawing air and lose its warranty
Surface contamination could enter the well through those openings
Algae will begin growing throughout the aquifer
correct_answer_text: Surface contamination could enter the well through those openings

question: A clearwell provides 45 minutes of contact time at a chlorine residual of 0.9 mg/L. What is the CT value?
options: 4.05 mg·min/L
405.00 mg·min/L
50.00 mg·min/L
40.50 mg·min/L
correct_answer_text: 40.50 mg·min/L

question: The secondary clarifier blanket is rising toward the weirs, but the MLSS is at the low end of the plant's range and the SVI is good at 95. What is the best first adjustment?
options: Increase the RAS rate to move settled solids out of the clarifier and back to the aeration basin faster
Increase the WAS rate to pull the total solids inventory down before the blanket reaches the surface in the entire system
Decrease the RAS rate so the clarifier has more quiet time for the blanket to compact on the bottom
Increase the basin air supply, because a rising blanket with a good SVI is usually caused by low DO
correct_answer_text: Increase the RAS rate to move settled solids out of the clarifier and back to the aeration basin faster

question: An operator plans to draw sludge out of a fixed-cover digester much faster than gas is being produced. Why is this an equipment concern?
options: The sludge draw-off line will plug where it leaves the tank
The heat exchanger will overheat the remaining digester sludge
A vacuum can form under the cover, damaging the cover and seals or drawing air into the digester
The mixing system will lose prime and stop circulating gas
correct_answer_text: A vacuum can form under the cover, damaging the cover and seals or drawing air into the digester

question: A critical pump is down and its seal kit is not on the shelf, though records show one in stock. Which inventory practice would have prevented this?
options: Ordering two of every part the plant has ever used, regardless of need
Storing all spare parts in one locked room that only one person can open
Recording new parts only when the storeroom clerk returns from vacation
Cycle counts that compare shelf stock with records and flag any mismatch
correct_answer_text: Cycle counts that compare shelf stock with records and flag any mismatch

question: After a bacteriological sample is prepared, where should it go without unnecessary delay?
options: Into a controlled incubator suited to the coliform method being used
Onto the open bench, where room conditions are adequate for growth
Into a refrigerator, where the cold will preserve the organisms
Into direct sunlight, where warmth will speed up the test result
correct_answer_text: Into a controlled incubator suited to the coliform method being used

question: A detector shows low oxygen at the bottom of a wet well. What should the entry team do first?
options: Enter quickly to finish the job before conditions get any worse during the day
Send one worker in without ventilation to check if the reading was a mistake
Have the entrant hold their breath while descending to the bottom of the wet well
Stop entry, ventilate the space from outside, and retest the atmosphere before anyone enters
correct_answer_text: Stop entry, ventilate the space from outside, and retest the atmosphere before anyone enters

question: What is the main purpose of a well's sanitary seal and casing?
options: To increase the well's yield by opening more water-bearing zones
To keep surface contamination from entering the well
To warm the groundwater before it reaches the pump
To hold the pump motor in place below ground
correct_answer_text: To keep surface contamination from entering the well

question: Light, fluffy floc is carrying over from the clarifier onto the filters, shortening filter runs. Which adjustment best addresses the cause?
options: Increase the filter backwash rate so the beds are cleaned more often
Improve coagulation and flocculation so floc is denser and settles better
Raise the chlorine dose sharply to break down the floating floc mass
Skip the sedimentation step and send floc straight to the filters
correct_answer_text: Improve coagulation and flocculation so floc is denser and settles better

question: One of three aerators in an aerated lagoon trips off and stays off for days. Solids begin settling in that corner and odors develop there, while the rest of the lagoon looks normal. Why?
options: That zone lost both its oxygen supply and its mixing
The remaining aerators are now mixing that corner too violently
The settled solids are being pushed there by the clarifier scum baffle
The lagoon liner in that corner has started leaking treated effluent outward
correct_answer_text: That zone lost both its oxygen supply and its mixing

question: What does the rotameter on a gas chlorinator show the operator?
options: The rate at which chlorine gas is being fed
The weight of the chlorine container in use
The pressure inside the chlorine container
The temperature of the chlorine feed room
correct_answer_text: The rate at which chlorine gas is being fed

question: Backup batteries for controls are found with low electrolyte and corroded terminals during inspection. What should be done?
options: Leave them alone, since backup batteries are only checked after a power failure
Disconnect the battery bank so the charger cannot overheat the corroded terminals
Clean the terminals, restore electrolyte to the proper level, and test the batteries
Add tap water until each cell overflows, then wipe the tops dry with a shop rag
correct_answer_text: Clean the terminals, restore electrolyte to the proper level, and test the batteries

question: Why should a DPD color result be read promptly once the color develops?
options: The reagent continues to grow stronger the longer it sits in the sample
Prompt reading prevents the sample from becoming a bacteriological hazard
The developed color can change or fade with time, altering the reading
The color becomes permanent after one minute and can no longer be read
correct_answer_text: The developed color can change or fade with time, altering the reading

question: A tanker arrives with a chemical delivery the plant was expecting. What should happen first?
options: The driver checks in, the delivery is verified, and staff direct the unloading process
The driver unloads wherever the hose reaches while staff finish their other rounds
The driver is given a plant key so future deliveries can be made without checking in
The driver drains the remaining heel of the last product into the new storage tank
correct_answer_text: The driver checks in, the delivery is verified, and staff direct the unloading process

question: Wellhead protection is primarily concerned with which activity?
options: Painting well houses to match surrounding buildings so the site blends in much better
Scheduling pump maintenance for the lowest-demand hours
Testing finished water at customer taps
Controlling land use near wells so contaminants are kept away from the source
correct_answer_text: Controlling land use near wells so contaminants are kept away from the source

question: A gravity filter has developed surging flow and uneven distribution, and air bubbles are seen rising in the bed. Head conditions in the filter have gone negative. What problem is this describing?
options: Mud ball formation deep in the support gravel
Air binding caused by negative head releasing dissolved air in the bed
Normal ripening after a backwash, which always produces air bubbles and surging flow
A broken influent baffle in the upstream clarifier
correct_answer_text: Air binding caused by negative head releasing dissolved air in the bed

question: A digester shows rising volatile acids while alkalinity is being consumed and gas production is falling. What is the best first response?
options: Increase the feed rate sharply
Drain half the digester at once
Double the seed sludge added hourly
Reduce or pause feeding and check temperature and mixing while alkalinity recovers
correct_answer_text: Reduce or pause feeding and check temperature and mixing while alkalinity recovers

question: A circular clarifier's rake turns at normal speed and drive torque is normal, but streaks of sludge are left on the floor behind the scraper arms. What is the most likely cause?
options: The rubber squeegee blades on the scraper arms are worn down and no longer wipe the floor clean as they pass
The influent to the basin has become too warm, which makes settled sludge too slippery for the rake to move
The effluent launder has too much capacity, so sludge is being pulled off the floor faster than it can settle
The drive motor is turning the rake slightly too fast for any blade to make contact with the basin floor
correct_answer_text: The rubber squeegee blades on the scraper arms are worn down and no longer wipe the floor clean as they pass

question: A feed pump fails during the night and a technician repairs it the next morning to return it to service. What type of maintenance was performed?
options: Preventive maintenance on a fixed schedule before any failure
Corrective maintenance — repair after failure
Predictive maintenance
Valve exercising
correct_answer_text: Corrective maintenance — repair after failure

question: Why is sodium thiosulfate placed in sterile bacteriological sample bottles?
options: To neutralize chlorine in the sample at collection
To feed coliform bacteria so they multiply during transport
To produce a pink color for chlorine testing
To preserve hardness for EDTA titration
correct_answer_text: To neutralize chlorine in the sample at collection

question: A severe freeze and winter storm are forecast to reach the plant within two days. What is the best preparation?
options: Drain all storage tanks completely so that no water remains anywhere to freeze solid
Send all operators home early and leave the plant unstaffed until the storm has passed
Open every building door to let warmer outside air circulate freely around the piping
Protect exposed piping from freezing, check generator fuel, and confirm chemical stocks
correct_answer_text: Protect exposed piping from freezing, check generator fuel, and confirm chemical stocks

question: Raw water entering the plant has a strong algae-related odor, rising daytime pH, and filters are clogging faster than usual. What condition should the operator suspect first?
options: A broken well casing allowing surface water in
Zebra mussels blocking the intake screens completely
An algae bloom in the source water
A leaking chlorine cylinder at the plant
correct_answer_text: An algae bloom in the source water

question: A clarifier performs well when sludge is wasted a little at a time on a regular schedule, but poorly when wasting is skipped for days. Why does the schedule matter?
options: Scheduled wasting adds fresh coagulant to the basin each time the sludge valve is opened up fully
Regular wasting keeps the blanket depth controlled so solids do not build up and carry over
Regular wasting warms the basin water so floc settles faster during cold weather periods
Skipping wasting raises the water level so the effluent launders stay submerged and quiet
correct_answer_text: Regular wasting keeps the blanket depth controlled so solids do not build up and carry over

question: Dye testing shows part of the flow crosses the chlorine contact basin in a few minutes while the rest takes much longer. What problem does this show?
options: Over-chlorination caused by water staying too long in a well-baffled basin
A chlorine demand of zero throughout the entire contact basin volume
Short-circuiting that cuts effective contact time
Excessive sludge digestion taking place inside the chlorine contact basin
correct_answer_text: Short-circuiting that cuts effective contact time

question: What is the purpose of the safety relief valve on an air compressor receiver tank?
options: To drain water from the bottom of the receiver at the end of shift
To supply instrument air to the control panels at a steady pressure
To vent the tank at a set pressure before the tank can be over-pressurized
To silence the noise made when the compressor unloads at cut-out
correct_answer_text: To vent the tank at a set pressure before the tank can be over-pressurized

question: Water weeps steadily from the stem of an isolation valve each time it is operated. What is the first reasonable maintenance step?
options: Snug the packing gland nuts evenly, a little at a time
Replace the entire valve body during the same shift
Weld the stem to the bonnet to seal the leak path shut
Ignore it, since stem leaks always stop on their own
correct_answer_text: Snug the packing gland nuts evenly, a little at a time

question: During a DPD chlorine test the pink color flashes and then fades almost completely, and the reading comes out near zero. What is the most likely explanation?
options: The sample contains no chlorine at all and the reagent is working exactly as it should be expected to
The chlorine level is very high and is bleaching the DPD color, giving a false low result
The colorimeter lamp is failing and should be replaced before any more tests are run
The sample was too cold, which prevents the DPD reagent from reacting with chlorine
correct_answer_text: The chlorine level is very high and is bleaching the DPD color, giving a false low result

question: When a water quality violation occurs, what must the utility do for the public?
options: Keep the violation internal until the next annual picnic
Provide public notification of the violation
Notify only customers who call to complain
Post the violation only inside the plant office
correct_answer_text: Provide public notification of the violation

question: A well that once produced strong flow now needs much more drawdown for the same yield, and its specific capacity has fallen steadily over several years. What does this pattern most likely indicate?
options: The aquifer is gaining water and the pump should be run much less often each day
The well screen or surrounding formation is clogging and rehabilitation is needed
The pump motor is oversized and the well itself is performing better than it once did
The static water level has risen and no further well evaluation is needed at all
correct_answer_text: The well screen or surrounding formation is clogging and rehabilitation is needed

question: What does the underdrain system beneath a rapid sand filter bed do?
options: It adds coagulant evenly across the whole surface of the filter bed
It measures head loss and signals when backwashing is needed
It removes settled sludge from the bottom of the clarifier
It collects filtered water and distributes backwash water evenly
correct_answer_text: It collects filtered water and distributes backwash water evenly

question: A primary clarifier receives wastewater with 220 mg/L TSS and produces an effluent of 66 mg/L TSS. What is the percent removal?

Solids are settling and building up in a flow equalization basin, and odors are increasing near the basin. Inspection shows one of the basin mixers has stopped running. Why does the stopped mixer explain the problem?
options: Mixers normally pump the basin contents to the clarifiers, so a stopped mixer blocks all forward flow through the plant each day
Mixers normally add chlorine to the basin, so a stopped mixer leaves the stored wastewater completely without any disinfection
Mixers normally heat the basin contents, so a stopped mixer lets the stored wastewater cool down and thicken into heavy sludge
Mixers keep solids suspended so they move on with the flow; without mixing, solids settle out in the basin and begin to turn septic
correct_answer_text: Mixers keep solids suspended so they move on with the flow; without mixing, solids settle out in the basin and begin to turn septic

question: Why must a standby generator be exercised regularly under load rather than only started briefly with no load?
options: To calibrate the turbidity analyzer
To exercise nearby distribution valves on schedule
To prove it can carry plant load, keep moving parts lubricated, and reveal problems before an outage
To prime all centrifugal pumps at once
correct_answer_text: To prove it can carry plant load, keep moving parts lubricated, and reveal problems before an outage

question: Why should an operator collect a generous volume of sample rather than only the few drops needed for a single test?
options: Extra volume allows repeat analyses and quality-control checks if a result is questioned
A larger volume makes the sample stay fresh for a much longer holding time in the bottle
Extra sample volume raises the concentration of the substance being measured
A generous volume lets the analyst skip calibrating the test instrument
correct_answer_text: Extra volume allows repeat analyses and quality-control checks if a result is questioned

question: Which practice best reduces exposure to pathogens in wastewater?
options: Eating lunch in the process area to save time during a busy operating shift
Wearing the same work gloves while eating and while handling wastewater samples
Touching the face with process gloves before washing at the end of the shift
Washing hands, covering wounds, and not eating in process areas
correct_answer_text: Washing hands, covering wounds, and not eating in process areas

question: During a drought the reservoir level drops close to the raw water pump suction and the pumps begin to lose prime and surge. What is the most likely cause?
options: The intake water has become too hard for the pumps to move
The low source level is starving the pump suction
Geosmin from algae has coated the pump impellers with slime film
The reservoir has turned over and filled the pumps with warm air
correct_answer_text: The low source level is starving the pump suction

question: Finished water leaving a plant is undersaturated and mildly corrosive, and metal release complaints are increasing. Which adjustment addresses the underlying stability problem?
options: Feed more coagulant so a thicker floc coats the inside of the pipes and forms a protective lining
Adjust pH and alkalinity so the water is brought closer to calcium carbonate balance
Raise the filter rate so water spends less time in the plant
Switch the disinfectant to ultraviolet light at the plant outlet
correct_answer_text: Adjust pH and alkalinity so the water is brought closer to calcium carbonate balance

question: A system holds 12,000 lb of solids under aeration, and 1,000 lb/day of solids leave in the waste sludge and effluent combined. What is the MCRT?
options: 0.08 days
8 days
24 days
12 days
correct_answer_text: 12 days

question: Why does sodium hypochlorite solution kept in storage gradually lose its available chlorine strength?
options: The chlorine settles to the bottom of the tank and cannot be pumped out
The solution breaks down over time, and heat and sunlight speed up the loss
The tank walls absorb the chlorine until the solution becomes plain water
The solution gains water from the air until it is too dilute to disinfect
correct_answer_text: The solution breaks down over time, and heat and sunlight speed up the loss

question: Which pairing correctly distinguishes two common chemical-feed arrangements?
options: Dry feeders deliver vapor; solution feeders deliver only air
Both dry and solution feeders are types of check valves
Dry feeders are used only on generators; solution feeders only on motors, with each serving one equipment type
Dry feeders dispense dry chemical, while solution feed systems feed a chemical dissolved in water
correct_answer_text: Dry feeders dispense dry chemical, while solution feed systems feed a chemical dissolved in water

question: An analyst reads an iron test immediately, well before the full color-development period, and gets a surprisingly low result. What went wrong?
options: Iron color develops instantly, so the low result must mean the sample was diluted
Waiting longer would destroy the color, so early readings are always more accurate
The color had not fully developed, so the reading understated the iron present
The reagent reacted with the glassware instead of with the iron in the sample
correct_answer_text: The color had not fully developed, so the reading understated the iron present

question: A treatment chemical spills on the plant floor during unloading. What guides the operators' first actions?
options: The chemical supplier's advertising brochure
The previous month's production schedule
The facility emergency response plan for spills
Guessing based on the color of the spilled chemical
correct_answer_text: The facility emergency response plan for spills

question: What is saltwater intrusion in a coastal groundwater source?
options: Road salt washing off highways into a reservoir in the winter
Treated water leaking from storage tanks back into the aquifer
Seawater moving inland into the aquifer and reaching wells
Ocean spray settling on the roof of a covered finished tank
correct_answer_text: Seawater moving inland into the aquifer and reaching wells

question: Tracer results show water reaches a clearwell outlet much sooner than its volume suggests it should. What is the most appropriate fix?
options: Raise the chlorine dose and accept the short path, since dose alone determines disinfection outcome
Improve baffling so incoming water follows a longer path instead of short-circuiting across
Lower the clearwell level permanently so the short path carries far less water each day
Remove the existing baffles so the flow can spread evenly across the whole clearwell floor
correct_answer_text: Improve baffling so incoming water follows a longer path instead of short-circuiting across

question: A chlorine dose of 4.6 mg/L is applied to treated effluent and the measured residual after contact is 1.2 mg/L. What is the chlorine demand?
options: 3.4 mg/L
5.8 mg/L
1.2 mg/L
4.6 mg/L
correct_answer_text: 3.4 mg/L

question: What does a pulsation dampener do on a diaphragm metering pump discharge?
options: It increases the stroke length of the pump head
It filters solids out of the chemical solution
It smooths the pulsing flow into a steadier stream
It measures the total chemical fed each day there now
correct_answer_text: It smooths the pulsing flow into a steadier stream

question: A pump motor repeatedly trips on overload shortly after starting. Which checks are most appropriate?
options: Check for a clogged or binding pump, excessive load, and electrical or mechanical faults rather than repeatedly resetting the trip
Reset the overload repeatedly and walk away
Remove the overload device
Spray the motor windings with water while it runs
correct_answer_text: Check for a clogged or binding pump, excessive load, and electrical or mechanical faults rather than repeatedly resetting the trip

question: A microscopic exam of mixed liquor shows healthy floc with many stalked ciliates. What does this most likely indicate?
options: Good operation with a well-developed, stable biomass and healthy floc structure
A very young, high food-to-mass sludge with mostly free-swimming ciliates and flagellates and very little formed floc present
Complete loss of the biomass
Severe filamentous bulking only
correct_answer_text: Good operation with a well-developed, stable biomass and healthy floc structure

question: A pump must be opened up for seal replacement. What must be done before the mechanic begins the work?
options: Run the pump briefly to confirm it still works
Lock out and tag out the equipment's energy sources so it cannot start
Leave the starter in automatic so the pump can be tested quickly while its casing is open
Remove only the coupling guard and begin
correct_answer_text: Lock out and tag out the equipment's energy sources so it cannot start

question: During a sanitary survey, which finding would be recorded as a source-water risk?
options: A damaged well seal with surface runoff ponding near the wellhead
A freshly painted fence around the plant site
A complete set of daily operating logs
A calibrated turbidimeter on the laboratory bench
correct_answer_text: A damaged well seal with surface runoff ponding near the wellhead

question: Why do plants insulate, drain, or heat-trace exposed process lines before freezing weather?
options: To keep chemical solutions warm enough that their feed pumps never need calibration again
To prevent algae from growing on the outside surfaces of pipes during the winter months
To keep water in the lines from freezing, expanding, and damaging pipes or interrupting flow
To raise the temperature of raw water so coagulation reactions proceed much faster daily
correct_answer_text: To keep water in the lines from freezing, expanding, and damaging pipes or interrupting flow

question: A plant at 0.8 MGD needs a 12 mg/L dose of a ferric product that is 80% pure. How many pounds per day of the product must be fed?
options: 80.1 lb/day
64.1 lb/day
100.1 lb/day
correct_answer_text: 100.1 lb/day

question: In a solid-bowl centrifuge, what is the differential speed?
options: The difference in rotational speed between the bowl and the scroll conveyor
The difference between the feed rate and the centrate discharge rate
The difference in temperature between the cake and the centrate streams
The difference in polymer dose between two machines running in parallel
correct_answer_text: The difference in rotational speed between the bowl and the scroll conveyor

question: A plant needs to meter a conductive process stream with no moving parts and almost no head loss. Which meter type fits best?
options: A magnetic meter, which senses voltage induced by the moving water
A venturi meter, which adds a long throat section to the pipe run
A propeller meter, which spins freely in the center of the stream
A positive displacement meter, which traps set volumes of water
correct_answer_text: A magnetic meter, which senses voltage induced by the moving water

question: Effluent phosphorus rises after a chemical feed pump loses prime, while influent phosphorus is unchanged. What is the best use of these lab results?
options: Restore the phosphorus removal chemical feed, verify the pump output, and confirm recovery with follow-up phosphorus results
Ignore them because influent is stable
Stop all sampling for phosphorus
Increase wasting with no feed check
correct_answer_text: Restore the phosphorus removal chemical feed, verify the pump output, and confirm recovery with follow-up phosphorus results

question: Why are inspection and maintenance records kept for safety equipment such as gas detectors and eyewash stations?
options: They are kept mainly to show auditors a thick binder of paperwork, and the actual condition of the equipment matters far less than having the forms filled in
They document that equipment was checked and maintained, reveal overdue items, and prove the equipment can be relied on in an emergency
They replace the need to actually inspect the equipment
They are needed only after an injury has occurred
correct_answer_text: They document that equipment was checked and maintained, reveal overdue items, and prove the equipment can be relied on in an emergency

question: Manganese in source water typically causes which problem?
options: Bright red water after aeration
A milky white appearance that clears from the bottom up
Excessive foaming at customer taps
Black or brown water and dark staining
correct_answer_text: Black or brown water and dark staining

question: What is the main purpose of sampling taps installed between treatment process units?
options: To provide drinking water for plant staff without using the finished-water plumbing
To let operators check the performance of each individual step in the treatment train
To drain each basin quickly whenever the plant needs to be taken out of service fast
To supply wash water for cleaning laboratory glassware between analytical test runs
correct_answer_text: To let operators check the performance of each individual step in the treatment train

question: An aerobic digester's volatile solids reduction has fallen off, the contents smell sour, and a portable meter shows dissolved oxygen near zero throughout the tank. What should be evaluated first?
options: Whether the digester is being decanted too often during the week
Whether the aeration system is actually delivering air to the tank
Whether the sludge feed pumps are painted the correct safety color
Whether the drying beds downstream are being loaded too deeply now
correct_answer_text: Whether the aeration system is actually delivering air to the tank

question: An operator finds large amounts of organic material settling out in a velocity-controlled grit channel along with the grit, and the collected grit smells septic. What is the most likely cause?
options: The channel velocity is too high, so the grit is being scoured through
The channel velocity is too low, allowing lighter organics to settle
The influent contains too little grit for the channel to work properly
The grit channel is too short for the plant's peak hourly flow rate
correct_answer_text: The channel velocity is too low, allowing lighter organics to settle

question: A high-level alarm sounds for a storage tank and water is reported running from its overflow. What should the operator do first?
options: Silence the alarm and wait one full day to see whether the level settles on its own by itself
Open the tank hatch and climb up to look inside while the water is still overflowing
Verify the tank level locally, check the inlet and altitude valve, and notify a supervisor
Drain the tank completely to the distribution system before checking any equipment
correct_answer_text: Verify the tank level locally, check the inlet and altitude valve, and notify a supervisor

question: An analyst writes a wrong digit on a bench sheet. What is the proper way to fix it?
options: Erase the entry completely so the sheet shows no trace of the mistake
Cover the error with correction fluid and write the new value over it
Rewrite the entire bench sheet and destroy the original page
Draw one line through the error, write the correction, and initial it
correct_answer_text: Draw one line through the error, write the correction, and initial it

question: An intrusion alarm activates at an unstaffed storage tank site overnight. What is the appropriate response?
options: Treat it as a security event, respond under the facility plan, and check the site for tampering before returning it to normal service
Ignore it because alarms are usually false and do not check the site
Disable the alarm system permanently
Open all hatches remotely to ventilate the tank
correct_answer_text: Treat it as a security event, respond under the facility plan, and check the site for tampering before returning it to normal service

question: On a sunny afternoon during an algae bloom, a reservoir's surface pH is noticeably higher than it was at dawn. What is the most likely cause?
options: Algae are photosynthesizing in daylight, which raises the pH
The reservoir has turned over and mixed cold bottom water to the surface
Iron in the water has oxidized and precipitated
Groundwater inflow has diluted the reservoir overnight
correct_answer_text: Algae are photosynthesizing in daylight, which raises the pH

question: Water flows through a channel with a cross-sectional area of 3 square feet at a velocity of 2 feet per second. What is the flow in gallons per minute?
options: 6.00 gpm

question: A plant at 0.5 MGD needs a 10 mg/L dose of a chemical that is 65% pure. How many pounds per day of the product must be fed?
options: 41.7 lb/day
64.2 lb/day
27.1 lb/day
6.4 lb/day
correct_answer_text: 64.2 lb/day

question: What does a foot valve at the bottom of a pump suction line do?
options: It acts as a check valve that keeps the suction line full of liquid so the pump stays primed
It grinds solids entering the suction line so the impeller cannot be damaged by debris of any size that enters the pump
It measures the depth of liquid in the wet well and sends the reading to the controls
It throttles the suction flow so the pump can never draw the wet well completely dry
correct_answer_text: It acts as a check valve that keeps the suction line full of liquid so the pump stays primed

question: What is fuel polishing for a standby generator's stored diesel?
options: Circulating the stored fuel through filters to remove water and contaminants
Adding dye to the fuel so leaks in the day tank are easier to spot later
Heating the fuel before startup so the engine reaches full load faster
Mixing fresh fuel into the old fuel each month so both batches age evenly over time
correct_answer_text: Circulating the stored fuel through filters to remove water and contaminants

question: What is the purpose of running a duplicate sample in the laboratory?
options: To double the reported result so that low values are easier for reviewers to read and compare
To use up older reagents before they pass their printed expiration dates
To check the precision of the method by seeing whether two analyses of one sample agree
To provide a backup bottle in case the first sample container is broken
correct_answer_text: To check the precision of the method by seeing whether two analyses of one sample agree

question: A multi-gas detector fails its bump test before a manhole entry. What is the correct action?
options: Use it anyway if it worked correctly during the previous shift entry
Do not use it for entry; calibrate it or replace it with a working unit
Wave it in fresh air for a minute and then proceed with the planned entry
Rely on odor alone for that entry since the crew is experienced and trained
correct_answer_text: Do not use it for entry; calibrate it or replace it with a working unit

question: A storm doubles raw water turbidity at the plant intake within a few hours. What is the best immediate operator response?
options: Keep all chemical doses unchanged until the next scheduled round
Check coagulation with jar testing and adjust chemical doses
Bypass sedimentation and send the storm water straight to filters
Shut the plant down for a week whenever turbidity rises after rain
correct_answer_text: Check coagulation with jar testing and adjust chemical doses

question: Where is an oxidant for iron and manganese control normally fed in the treatment train?
options: After disinfection, so the oxidized metals can settle quietly inside the clearwell tank
Inside the finished-water storage tank, so oxidation finishes while the water is stored
At the laboratory bench only, since oxidants are used solely for testing water samples
Ahead of filtration, so the oxidized metals can be captured and removed by the filters
correct_answer_text: Ahead of filtration, so the oxidized metals can be captured and removed by the filters

question: A plant is switching dewatering polymer products. Three products are available at different prices. How should the operator choose among them?
options: Bench-test each on the actual sludge and compare floc, water release, and capture
Choose the cheapest product per pound, since all polymers perform the same
Choose the product the previous operator used at a different plant years ago
Run each product for a full month on the press and judge by the cake color alone
correct_answer_text: Bench-test each on the actual sludge and compare floc, water release, and capture

question: Why are online chlorine analyzer readings periodically compared with a grab sample tested on a bench or portable kit?
options: To use up reagent before its expiration date arrives
To prove the grab kit is more accurate than the analyzer
To verify the analyzer is still reading accurately between calibrations
To satisfy the sample courier who transports compliance samples who picks it up later in the same shift
correct_answer_text: To verify the analyzer is still reading accurately between calibrations

question: Discharge pressure rises on a chemical feed line, yet a positive-displacement metering pump continues delivering nearly the same volume per stroke. Why is this expected?
options: Positive-displacement pumps stop whenever pressure changes
Centrifugal pumps always behave this way
Gate valves regulate the pump's strokes
Each stroke traps and moves a set volume, so delivery stays nearly constant despite pressure changes
correct_answer_text: Each stroke traps and moves a set volume, so delivery stays nearly constant despite pressure changes

question: Halfway through a shift, a turbidimeter check with a known standard reads well off its expected value. What should the operator do?
options: Continue testing as usual and simply note the observed difference in the margin of the bench sheet
Recheck the standard and cuvette, then recalibrate the instrument if the error is confirmed
Adjust all of the morning's sample results by the size of the observed difference
Discard the standard, since a disagreement means the standard itself must be wrong
correct_answer_text: Recheck the standard and cuvette, then recalibrate the instrument if the error is confirmed

question: What is the main purpose of the monthly operations report?
options: It summarizes flows, treatment performance, and notable events so management and regulators can see how the plant operated
It replaces the need for daily logs during the month, because the monthly summary contains everything the daily records would have shown anyway
It is used only to schedule employee vacations
It lists chemicals the plant hopes to buy next year
correct_answer_text: It summarizes flows, treatment performance, and notable events so management and regulators can see how the plant operated

question: How does cold winter source water generally affect treatment compared with warm water?
options: Chemical reactions speed up and visible floc forms much faster
Disinfection works faster with no change in chemical dose
Settling improves greatly because the water is less dense
Chemical reactions slow and settling can become harder
correct_answer_text: Chemical reactions slow and settling can become harder

question: A clarifier receives water at 45 NTU and produces settled water at 3 NTU. What is the percent removal across the clarifier?
When an operator decants an aerobic digester, the supernatant starts out clear but turns cloudy with solids partway through the draw. What should the operator do?
options: Keep decanting until the tank is nearly empty to save time later
Increase the decant rate so the cloudy portion passes more quickly
Stop decanting when solids begin appearing in the supernatant
Mix the digester vigorously while decanting to even out the solids
correct_answer_text: Stop decanting when solids begin appearing in the supernatant

question: A vacuum-operated gas chlorinator stops feeding even though the chlorine container still holds chlorine. What should the operator check first?
options: The chlorine residual analyzer mounted on the effluent line
The sodium hypochlorite level in the day tank in the same room
The injector and its vacuum lines, since loss of injector vacuum stops gas feed in this design
The water level in the contact basin at the outlet weir
correct_answer_text: The injector and its vacuum lines, since loss of injector vacuum stops gas feed in this design

question: What does a check valve do in a piping system?
options: It provides precise throttling of flow
It vents air automatically at high points whenever air collects in a pipeline
It isolates a section of pipe for repair
It prevents reverse flow when a pump stops or pressure reverses
correct_answer_text: It prevents reverse flow when a pump stops or pressure reverses

question: How does a COD result generally compare to a BOD result for the same wastewater sample?
options: COD is slower than BOD and always lower for every type of wastewater sample tested
COD and BOD are always identical
COD takes five full days to run
COD is faster and generally higher
correct_answer_text: COD is faster and generally higher

question: What does ensuring compliance with applicable regulations mean in daily plant operation?
options: Following permit conditions only when an inspector is scheduled to visit
Choosing whichever discharge limit is easiest to meet
Treating the permit as general guidance that experienced operators may override whenever they judge that plant conditions justify a different approach
Operating within the plant's permit limits and required procedures every day, and documenting that performance
correct_answer_text: Operating within the plant's permit limits and required procedures every day, and documenting that performance

question: Besides taste and odor problems, algae blooms commonly cause which operating problem?
options: Higher groundwater levels in nearby wells
Shorter filter runs
Cracks in the well sanitary seal
Loss of prime in chemical feed pumps
correct_answer_text: Shorter filter runs

question: A plant applies a chlorine dosage of 3.4 mg/L and measures a residual of 0.8 mg/L. What is the chlorine demand?
Effluent phosphorus is above the plant's target, and the plant removes phosphorus by dosing alum ahead of the clarifiers. How should the operator set the alum dose?
options: Use the same dose reported by a neighboring plant
Dose at a fixed rate per million gallons regardless of results
Run jar tests and adjust the dose based on treated-water results
Set the dose by the color of the mixed liquor and raise it whenever the clarifier effluent looks cloudy in the morning
correct_answer_text: Run jar tests and adjust the dose based on treated-water results

question: On a belt filter press, the belt keeps wandering to one side and sludge squeezes out at the edges. What should the operator check first?
options: Belt tracking and tension adjustments on the press
The color of the polymer being fed to the sludge today
The wash water hose stored beside the press unit
The age of the press building's overhead lighting
correct_answer_text: Belt tracking and tension adjustments on the press

question: To reduce the risk of water hammer when shutting down a large line, what should an operator do?
options: Close valves slowly and in a controlled manner
Close valves as fast as possible
Stop all pumps at once without warning
Remove all air-relief valves from the line completely
correct_answer_text: Close valves slowly and in a controlled manner

question: Which laboratory method is used to measure hardness?
options: DPD colorimetric test
Gravimetric filtration and weighing
Nephelometric light measurement
EDTA titration
correct_answer_text: EDTA titration

question: What is included in a routine facility security check?
options: Checking gates, doors, lighting, and signs of tampering or intrusion
Leaving gates open so delivery drivers can enter at any hour without calling
Turning off exterior lighting at night to save energy around the plant site
Removing locks from chemical storage areas for faster operator access at night
correct_answer_text: Checking gates, doors, lighting, and signs of tampering or intrusion

question: After heavy rain, a reservoir's raw water turns turbid and carries nutrients washed from fields and scattered septic systems across the watershed. This is mainly an example of what?
options: Point source contamination from a single pipe
A failure of the plant's filter backwash cycle
Contamination caused by reservoir turnover alone
Nonpoint source contamination
correct_answer_text: Nonpoint source contamination

question: Dye testing shows water short-circuits through a sedimentation basin well ahead of its theoretical detention time. Which fix best addresses this?
options: Increase the chlorine dose to make up for the lost contact time
Drain the basin and leave it empty until flows increase later
Improve baffling or inlet distribution so flow spreads evenly
Raise the sludge blanket so water must travel a longer path
correct_answer_text: Improve baffling or inlet distribution so flow spreads evenly

question: A belt press blinds quickly, cake releases poorly, and several wash-water nozzles are found plugged. What is the effect of restoring wash water?
options: Wash water dissolves polymer
Dry belts capture more solids
Wash water heats the sludge
Clean belts drain water better and release the pressed cake much more cleanly
correct_answer_text: Clean belts drain water better and release the pressed cake much more cleanly

question: Water is spraying from a pump's packing area instead of the slight drip that is normal. What should the operator do?
options: Tighten the gland fully until all leakage stops
Remove the packing so water can flow out freely
Ignore it because any leakage cools the shaft well enough
Adjust the gland evenly or plan packing replacement
correct_answer_text: Adjust the gland evenly or plan packing replacement

question: An inline pH meter's readings have begun to drift. Which calibration approach should the operator use?
options: Calibrate it with chlorine standards only, using residual solutions instead of pH buffers
Compare it only with a turbidity standard
Let it run until it fails completely
Calibrate it with standard buffer solutions, typically including pH 7 and pH 4 or 10
correct_answer_text: Calibrate it with standard buffer solutions, typically including pH 7 and pH 4 or 10

question: Influent TSS is 200 mg/L and effluent TSS is 30 mg/L. What is the percent removal across the plant?
options: 15 percent removal based only on the effluent value divided by the influent value alone
170 percent removal across the plant
70 percent removal across the plant
85 percent
correct_answer_text: 85 percent

question: A resident calls about a sewer odor near their home. What is the best operator response?
options: Hang up and refer all odor calls to a neighboring town's public works office
Listen, document the location and time, and follow the complaint procedure
Promise the odor will never occur again regardless of the investigation results
Tell the caller that odors are never caused by the collection system at all
correct_answer_text: Listen, document the location and time, and follow the complaint procedure

question: A utility wants to reduce the chance of contamination reaching its reservoir intake. Which action fits a source-water protection approach?
options: Waiting until contamination reaches the plant before acting, taking no steps in the watershed
Removing the intake screens so debris passes through
Working with landowners upstream to control runoff and risky activities in the watershed
Testing only finished water and ignoring the watershed
correct_answer_text: Working with landowners upstream to control runoff and risky activities in the watershed

question: A filter's effluent turbidity is 0.28 NTU and climbing, while the plant's operational goal is about 0.1 to 0.3 NTU. What is the best response?
options: Take no action, because any reading below 1 NTU is always acceptable
Shut the whole plant down immediately and drain the clearwell
Monitor closely and prepare to end the run if it keeps rising
Raise the filtration rate to dilute the turbidity in the flow
correct_answer_text: Monitor closely and prepare to end the run if it keeps rising

question: On a staged rotating biological contactor, the first-stage discs carry an unusually thick, heavy growth while later stages look thin, and overall BOD removal has fallen. What does this pattern indicate?
options: The last stage is stealing oxygen from the first stage at night
The shaft is turning too fast for any growth to attach to the discs
The first stage is receiving more organic load than it can handle
The clarifier ahead of the contactor is removing too many solids before the first stage
correct_answer_text: The first stage is receiving more organic load than it can handle

question: Thick green growth coats a clarifier's weirs and launder walls, and clumps of it keep appearing in the effluent during bright, sunny periods. What maintenance action addresses this?
options: Raise the sludge blanket so the growth stays submerged and out of the sunlight
Increase the rake speed so the scraper arms knock the growth off the weir plates
Clean the algae growth from the weirs and launders on a regular basis
Cover the effluent samples so the laboratory does not report the extra solids
correct_answer_text: Clean the algae growth from the weirs and launders on a regular basis

question: Why must a guard be in place over a rotating pump coupling before the unit runs?
options: It holds the two shafts in alignment while the pump is running
It reduces the noise the coupling makes at higher pump speeds
It catches lubricating oil thrown off the coupling each shift
It keeps hands, clothing, and tools away from the rotating parts
correct_answer_text: It keeps hands, clothing, and tools away from the rotating parts

question: A turbidity sample that was shaken vigorously shows tiny bubbles clinging to the cuvette walls. What should the analyst do?
options: Read it immediately, because bubbles clinging to the walls have no effect on scattered light
Add a drop of detergent so the bubbles break up and disperse quickly
Shake the sample harder so the bubbles become too small to matter
Let the sample stand briefly so bubbles clear before taking the reading
correct_answer_text: Let the sample stand briefly so bubbles clear before taking the reading

question: How should respirators be stored between uses?
options: On an open hook in the process area so they are close at hand
Cleaned, inspected, and kept in a sealed container or bag away from dust, moisture, and sunlight
In a toolbox together with oily rags, solvents, and spare tools, where they stay handy for whichever worker happens to need one next
Shared on a common shelf without cleaning so they are always ready
correct_answer_text: Cleaned, inspected, and kept in a sealed container or bag away from dust, moisture, and sunlight

question: A well yields 240 gpm with 30 ft of drawdown. What is the well's specific capacity?
options: 8.00 gpm/ft
0.13 gpm/ft
270.00 gpm/ft
correct_answer_text: 8.00 gpm/ft

question: How does a chloramine residual compare with a free chlorine residual?
options: It is a combined residual that is weaker as a disinfectant but lasts longer in the water
It is a free residual that disinfects faster than hypochlorous acid and is preferred for the fastest kill
It provides no residual at all once it leaves the plant
It forms only when ozone reacts with bromide in the water
correct_answer_text: It is a combined residual that is weaker as a disinfectant but lasts longer in the water

question: A settleometer shows 240 mL/L settled after 30 minutes and the MLSS is 2,400 mg/L. What is the SVI?
options: 100 mL/g
10 mL/g
correct_answer_text: 100 mL/g

question: Flow recorded at a Parshall flume has become erratic and does not match the water level operators see in the channel. The level sensor reads from a stilling well beside the flume, and the well is found full of grease and debris. What is the problem?
options: The flume throat has widened, so the stilling well is now the only accurate part of the installation
The recorded flow is erratic because operators are checking the channel level too many times a day
Grease and debris in the stilling well and its connecting port keep the well level from tracking the real channel level
The stilling well is supposed to stay full of debris so the sensor is cushioned from flow surges
correct_answer_text: Grease and debris in the stilling well and its connecting port keep the well level from tracking the real channel level

question: A portable generator is run just outside an open plant doorway during an outage, and staff inside feel headaches and dizziness. What is the danger and fix?
options: Diesel fumes are harmless but unpleasant; staff should open more doors so the smell clears faster for them
Carbon monoxide from the exhaust is drifting inside; move the generator farther away, exhaust pointing away
The generator is overloading the building circuits; staff should shed load until the symptoms pass on their own
Low oxygen from the plant's own ventilation is the cause; the generator should be moved inside the building
correct_answer_text: Carbon monoxide from the exhaust is drifting inside; move the generator farther away, exhaust pointing away

question: Free chlorine residual consists of:
options: Only chloramines formed after chlorine reacts with ammonia
Only chlorine demand
Calcium and magnesium ions
Hypochlorous acid (HOCl) plus hypochlorite ion (OCl-)
correct_answer_text: Hypochlorous acid (HOCl) plus hypochlorite ion (OCl-)

question: Why must operating records be kept for the full required retention period?
options: So operators have extra paperwork to complete whenever a shift happens to run slowly
So the utility can discard original lab results once a summary has been typed up neatly
So past performance can be verified, reviewed, and reported long after the work is done
So inspectors are given only the records from weeks when the plant ran especially well
correct_answer_text: So past performance can be verified, reviewed, and reported long after the work is done

question: What is the static water level in a well?
options: The water level in the well when it is not being pumped
The water level measured only while the pump is running at full capacity
The depth from the pump intake to the bottom of the well
The total depth of casing installed below ground
correct_answer_text: The water level in the well when it is not being pumped

question: A process pump delivers 900 gpm against a total head of 60 ft. What is the water horsepower?

In a settleometer left standing after the 30-minute reading, the settled sludge begins rising to the top in chunks after about 90 minutes, with small bubbles visible in it. What does this warn the operator about?
options: The sample was contaminated by grit, which always makes settled sludge float once the cylinder has stood for an hour
The mixed liquor needs more air in the cylinder, and shaking the sample hourly is the correct way to run the settling test
The rising proves the sludge is young and healthy, because only fresh sludge has enough energy to lift itself in the test
The sludge can denitrify and float in the clarifier the same way if it is held there too long, so blanket detention needs watching
correct_answer_text: The sludge can denitrify and float in the clarifier the same way if it is held there too long, so blanket detention needs watching

question: A centrifuge has developed rising vibration and drive torque, its cake is getting wetter, and solids are building up inside the bowl faster than they can be conveyed out. What internal condition do these signs point to?
options: The feed sludge has become too warm for the machine to process
The polymer day tank is due to be refilled before the next shift
The scroll conveyor's working edges are worn, so it moves solids out of the bowl less effectively
The centrate line is one size too small for the plant's peak flows that the plant sees during the wettest weeks of the year
correct_answer_text: The scroll conveyor's working edges are worn, so it moves solids out of the bowl less effectively

question: A high-use pump drips heavily at the shaft and wastes treated water. Which change most directly reduces that shaft leakage?
options: Tighten the packing gland down firmly until all visible dripping fully stops today
Run the pump at a higher speed to throw the water outward
Replace the worn packing with a mechanical seal on that pump
Add extra grease to the bearings beside the stuffing box
correct_answer_text: Replace the worn packing with a mechanical seal on that pump

question: What does the indicator in a hardness titration show the analyst?
options: Its color shows the exact calcium-to-magnesium ratio present in the sample
Its fading shows that the EDTA reagent has passed its expiration date
